question: The Xinjiang region, which was seen in the news due to the collapse of a gold mine, is located in which country?
solution:
The correct answer is __**China**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Xinjiang is located in the northwest of China.
 
• It is the largest province-level division of China and the 8th-largest country subdivision in the world.
 
• It borders the countries of Mongolia, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Afghanistan, Pakistan and India.
 
• It has a population of about 25 million. The majority of ethnic groups include Uyghur and Han Chinese, among others.
 
• It is known for its natural resources, including oil, natural gas, gold, and coal. It also has large farmlands where cotton, wheat, and fruits are grown.
 
• The region is culturally diverse, home to a mix of ethnicities including Uyghur, Kazakh, Tajik, Hui, Kyrgyz, Mongol, and more.
 
• Islam is the dominant religion among several ethnic groups, especially the Uyghurs and Kazakhs.
 
• It has been the subject of significant international attention due to allegations of human rights abuses against the Uyghur population by the Chinese government.
 
• It has several gold mines, and instances like mine collapses can often make it to the news due to the safety concerns associated with such incidents.
